params: a, b, c: point refs; name?

label: Tangent Plane
params: face: ref (cylinder, cone, sphere or torus); at?: [x,y,z] where it touches (default: the face pick); reference?: plane or planar face ref (the plane touches where the face turns towards it: parallel to it, on the side of `at`); angle?: expr (with reference, default 0 deg: turned that far about the face's axis; not on a sphere); name?

label: Plane Along Path
params: path: edge or sketch curve ref; t: expr, 0…1 along it (default 0.5); name? The plane is square to the path there

label: Perpendicular Plane
params: plane: plane or planar face ref; line: straight edge, sketch line or axis ref; name? The plane holds the line and is square to the plane

label: Flange
params: base: sketch + profiles? (rule?, flip?) | contour: sketch + curves (open chain of lines) + distance (rule?, flip?, reverse?) | edge: edges: [[x,y,z] on top/bottom edges, or {point: [x,y,z], angle?, height?} for an edge with its own angle and height] + height (along the flange, to its far edge), angle? (default 90 deg), radius? (default: rule), height_from?: outer|inner|tangent (where the height is measured from: the outer virtual sharp (default), the inner virtual sharp, or past 90 deg the line square to the flange touching the bend's outside (tangent; up to 90 deg the outer sharp)), position?: inside|outside|middle|material_outside|tangent (where the bend starts: the outer virtual sharp on the edge (default), the bend starting at the edge (bend_outside is the same), half way, the inner virtual sharp on the edge, or the bend's outer face tangent to the edge's face (below 90 deg the bend's end on that face)), flip?, body?, corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear and corner_relief? (size across): the relief at the corners these flanges make (default: the rule's); then?: [{angle?, height, flip?}] further bends (at most 16), each a flange on the far edge of the one before, flip: true turns that bend the other way (edge only); type?: base|edge|contour (default from the inputs); name?, body_name? (the new body). Thickness, K-factor and bend radius come from the rule (sheet.manage_rules); passing them here is refused, and so is the corner relief on a base or contour flange

label: Path Flange
params: edge: [x,y,z] on a top or bottom edge of the sheet; sketch + curves: an open chain of sketch lines drawn on a plane across that edge, from the edge out (each line one flange as long as the line, to the outer face from the virtual sharp; each corner one bend, turning the way the lines turn); radius? (default: rule); body?. One feature, one body

label: Perforate
params: diameter, pitch: expr; margin?: expr (clear of edges, cut-outs, bends and the outline; default: the diameter); pattern?: staggered (60°, default) | square; body?; sketch? + profiles? (the outline: closed profiles of a sketch on a face of the sheet; holes only inside them, out of their inner loops) - a perforation field over the whole flat sheet or inside the outline: holes in the flat pattern (perforations), the DXF (layer PERFORATION) and the measured volume, not cut into the B-rep (#732)

label: Hem
params: edges: [[x,y,z] on sheet edges]; length (to the outer face); gap? (inner radius, default: rule); flip?; body?

label: Fold
params: line: sketch + curve (a sketch line on the sheet's base face; followed when the sketch changes) or points: [[x,y,z], [x,y,z]]; angle? (default 90 deg); radius? (default: rule); position?: centerline|start|end|mould (where the line sits in the bend, default centerline); fixed?: [x,y,z] on the side that stays (default: the larger side); flip? (fold the other way); body?

label: Unfold
params: body? (default: the last sheet body) — all bends

label: Refold
params: body? (default: the last unfolded sheet)

label: Convert to Sheet Metal
params: body; face: [x,y,z] on its large flat face (a plate of even thickness; recesses in one face up to half the thickness deep, such as an engraved label, become pockets of the sheet), or that face's name from model.faces; rule?; bends?: [[x,y,z] on sharp edges] (a solid or a shelled body: `face` is the fixed face and the flat faces reached from it across these edges become the sheet; a shell keeps its thickness, a solid takes the rule's inward; edges between two of those faces that are no bends are cut open with the rule's gap; a point in the middle of a chamfer between two faces, or on a bend modelled with its radius (a cylinder between two flat faces tangent to it, either skin), makes it one bend of the rule's radius at their virtual sharp; the faces' holes become cut-outs and their engravings, up to half the thickness deep, pockets)

label: Sheet Metal Rules
params: name (new or existing); thickness?, k_factor?, bend_radius?, relief_width?, relief_depth?, corner_relief?, hem_gap?, gap? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's; gap: between flanges that meet at a corner, whose ends are closed toward each other at any angle); corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear (what is cut where two bends meet at a corner of the base: round and rectangular a relief `corner_relief` across; tear none, each bend's end is cut straight from the corner to its flange's end; default notch); angle_display?: bend|included (how the DXF bend notes read the bend angles: the bend angle, default, or the included angle left between the bend's sides, 180° less it; the bend table gives both, and a flange's `angle` is always the bend angle); active?: bool; delete?: bool

label: List Sheet Metal Rules
params: → rules with their expressions and values, and the active one

label: Create Flat Pattern
params: body? → flat size, outline loops and cut-outs (flat coordinates, as point lists), cutout_shapes (the same cut-outs exactly, in the same order: {circle: {center, radius}} for a round hole, else {segments: [{line: [a, b]} | {arc: {center, radius, start_deg, sweep_deg}} | {polyline: [...]}]}), pockets (with their own cutout_shapes), bend lines and the bend table

label: Export Flat Pattern as DXF
params: body?, path?, curves?: exact|arcs (default exact: an ellipse as ELLIPSE, splines, text outlines and other Béziers as SPLINE; arcs: tangent arcs and lines within 0.001 mm, for machines that read only those), text?: cut|etch (default cut: letters that text cut through the sheet are cut contours on layer TEXT; etch: single contours on layer ETCH and the sheet keeps its material there; text machined to a depth is always on ETCH), bend_notes?: bool (default false: a note beside each bend line on layer BEND_NOTES, `B1 UP 90%%d R1`, its angle the included angle when the body's rule has angle_display: included), note_height?: mm (default 3), bend_lines?: bool (default true; false leaves BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN out, for a cutter that would cut them), layers?: roles|single (default roles, the layers below; single: every entity on layer 0), per_body?: bool (a file for every sheet body, `<path>-<body>.dxf`, or their DXF texts without a path → files: [{body, path | dxf, bends}]; not with `body`) → DXF (AutoCAD 2000, mm): layers OUTLINE (the outer contour), CUT (what is cut out inside it), TEXT or ETCH (letters), BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN (dashed centre lines), BEND_NOTES, POCKET_<BOTTOM|TOP|INTERNAL>_Z<from>_TO_<to>_MM (one per side and depth) and PERFORATION; inner contours come before the outline

label: Export Bend Table
params: body?, format?: csv|json (default csv), path? → bend table in mm and degrees, including rule and flat centre-line coordinates; angle_deg is the bend angle and included_angle_deg the angle left between the bend's sides (180° less it); a bend that cut-outs split has a row for each piece

label: Boss
params: position: [x,y,z] on a face; direction? (default: out of the face); diameter, height; hole_diameter?, hole_depth? (default: to the face); draft? (angle), fillet? (root radius); ribs? (count), rib_thickness?, rib_length? (out from the wall), rib_offset? (below the top); body?

label: Lip
params: face: [x,y,z] on the rim face of a shelled body; width, height; type?: lip|groove; gap? (groove clearance); side?: inside|outside (which rim edge); body?

label: Snap Fit
params: position: [x,y,z] on a face; direction? (default: out of the face); hook: [x,y,z] (the catch's direction); length, thickness, width, catch_depth, catch_length; base_height? (extends the base below the face); new_body?: bool (make a separate body instead of joining); body?

label: Rest
params: position: [x,y,z] on a face (the rest's centre); direction? (default: out of the face); width (round: the diameter); length? (a rectangle, along `along`); along?: [x,y,z]; height; draft? (angle; default: the body's plastic rule); thickness? (wall of a hollow rest); body?

label: Manage Plastic Rules
params: name (library or new rule; a new one starts from `from`, default ABS (1.5mm)); from?; material?; thickness?, nominal_radius?, clearance?, knife_edge?, reveal_height?, thickness_variation?, draft?, max_thickness?, min_thickness?, min_draft? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's); active?: bool (rule for bodies without one); delete?: bool (a design rule; a library rule goes back to the library values)

label: Assign Plastic Rule
params: bodies: [names]; rule: name (empty: no rule) — plastic features on these bodies take its draft and clearance as defaults

label: List Plastic Rules
params: → rules with their expressions and values, the active rule and the rules assigned to bodies

label: Frame Member
params: sketch: the frame sketch (id or name; 2D or 3D); lines?: [curve ids] (one member each; default: every straight line drawn in the sketch: not construction, not projected or otherwise linked, not of no length); profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in")} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | profile_sketch: a sketch whose profile is the section, in its own x and y around its origin, with profiles?: picks as solid.extrude takes them (default: its material, nested loops alternating, so two circles make a tube); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point that sits on each line, default origin); angle?: angle expr (the profile turned about the line; default 0: its y as near world up as the line allows, a vertical member's x along world X); mirror?: bool (the profile mirrored across its y axis); name?; body_name? (what the members are named after, then numbered: `Rail`, `Rail (2)`…; default the profile's description, `Rect Tube 40x40x3`, or the profile sketch's name); names?: {line id: name} (names to keep, as Edit Feature keeps them). One body per line, from its start to its end; each member keeps its name when other lines are added or deleted. Returns the feature and the bodies it made

label: Profile Library
params: Returns kinds: [{kind, label, required, optional, example}]: the built-in profiles, each SolidCraft's own parametric definition

label: Profile Properties
params: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in")} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size); density?: kg/m³ (adds mass_per_m, kg/m). Returns profile (every default filled in), area (mm²), centroid [x,y] (mm, from the bounding box centre), ixx, iyy, ixy (mm⁴ about the centroid), width, height

label: Insert Profile
params: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in")} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size); at?: [x,y] (sketch mm, default the origin); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point placed on `at`: its origin, the default and a built-in profile's centre, its bounding box's centre, its centroid, or a corner or edge middle of its bounding box); angle?: radians, counter-clockwise; fixed?: bool (default true: the curves are locked, so solving the sketch keeps the shape); sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited). Returns the section as frame.profile.properties does. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Cycle Component Color
params: component: id or name; saves the next identification colour and enables Component Colors; shared by every instance, separate from appearances

label: Hide Component History
params: component: id or name; keeps the component's features in the design but leaves them out of the History bar (#10393)

label: Show Component History
params: component: id or name; puts a component's features back in the History bar after Hide Component History (#10393)

label: New Component
params: name?, parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); parent_path?: exact parent placement; activate?: bool (default true); grounded?: bool (default: true for the design's first part, false otherwise)

label: Create Components from Bodies
params: bodies: [names] → one new component per body, named after it

label: Activate Component
params: component: id or name (0 or "root" for the design); occurrence?, path?: exact placement used to author shared geometry

label: Edit in Place
params: component: id or name of a linked component; path?: its placement (occurrence ids, default its first) → in the app window: open the design it links in a tab of its own with the assembly drawn around it (component.finish_edit goes back); fails when it is not linked, the assembly has no file yet, something is open or running in it, or the file is missing, on a network location not allowed yet or open in another SolidCraft; asked during the agent's turn it opens once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere it only checks

label: Finish Edit
params: no parameters → in the app window: go back from the linked design edited in place to its assembly, which reads it again; fails while the design has unsaved changes (run file.save first) or something is open in it; asked during the agent's turn it finishes once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere nothing changes

label: List Components
params: compact?: bool (counts of bodies, features, sketches and construction planes instead of their names; occurrences leave out identity transforms; children as occurrence ids); bodies?: bool (with compact: body names, not their count)

label: Component Physical Properties
params: component?: id or name (default active); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Measures the first placement, or all placements for root, including pending moves; material-aware mass and center of mass in world coordinates; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 (the inertia tensor about the body's center of mass, world axes, from its tessellation) only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total.first_moment_g_mm (mass × center of mass), inertia_g_mm2 about the total center of mass, principal_moments_g_mm2 (smallest first) and principal_axes (unit, right-handed); with about, total.inertia_about {point, inertia_g_mm2}

label: Occurrence Physical Properties
params: occurrence: id or name; path?: [occurrence ids] (required if nested under multiple instances); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Physical properties of this placement in world coordinates, including pending moves; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total inertia as in component.properties

label: Rename Component
params: component, name

label: Delete Component
params: component: deletes it, its subcomponents, occurrences and features

label: Unlock Contents
params: component: removes the rigid joints that hold its contents together (an imported assembly's rigid group), so its parts move and take joints one by one → joints (the ids removed)

label: Move Bodies to Component
params: bodies: [names], component; component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance); from_path?: the placement of their component they move from (default: its only one, else its first, where its bodies have their own names)

label: Paste Bodies
params: bodies: [names, as the Browser shows them: a body seen in another placement of its component (`Cube (B:2)`) is copied from there]; component?: where the copies go (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance). Each copy stays where its body is in the world; the copies' names come back as `bodies`

label: Paste from Another Design
params: component?: where it goes (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one). Pastes what was copied in another design, at the same world coordinates: its bodies as imported bodies (no history) in one Import feature, or its components as independent copies with their history, appearances, joints and motion (as `component.paste_new`); the user parameters they use come along, renamed `w_2` when taken. A component that uses what isn't in it (another body, sketch or parameter) is refused, saying what. Returns `bodies` and `feature`, or the pasted components' `paths`

label: Move Sketches to Component
params: sketches: [ids or names], component; the sketches keep their own coordinates (component.move_features keeps them where they are in the world), except that a sketch on an exactly attached face stays where it is on the face

label: Move Sketches to Their Parts
params: sketches?: [ids or names] (default: every sketch in the design) → moved, stayed, sketches [{sketch, name, component, part}], kept [{sketch, name, code, reason}]. Each sketch whose plane is an exactly attached face of a part's body goes to that part, as component.move_sketches moves it, and stays where it is on the face; the others (on an origin, construction or fixed plane, on a body of the design itself, or already in their part) stay where they are. One undo step

label: Move Features to Component
params: features: [ids or names] (sketches too); component?: where they go (default: the active one) → moved, component, bodies. Ids, names and timeline order stay; the geometry stays where it is in the world; the bodies the features made move with them. Refused while the timeline is rolled back, for a component placed more than once, and for a move that would break a feature (nothing changes)

label: Move to Component
params: Moves placements, features and bodies into a component. occurrences?: [ids or paths], features?: [ids or names], bodies?: [names], component?: where they go (default: the active one), component_path?: its placement → component, occurrences, features, bodies (what moved). One undo step, all or nothing: placements move first (taking what they hold), then features (taking the bodies they made), then the bodies still elsewhere (a body transfer, which leaves its features behind)

label: Paste (Instance)
params: component (or occurrence): what to place again; path?: validates selected occurrence; parent?: component (default: the same parent); translate?: [x,y,z]; in_place?: bool (default false: the selected transform within the parent; true: where the selected placement is in the world, translate in world axes; a parent placed more than once is placed by parent_path?, else the active placement, and every instance gets the copy). Copies the selected effective transform, including pending moves

label: Paste New
params: component: independently copy its nested definition graph and history, materials and styles; occurrence?, path?: selected source placement; parent?: component the copy goes in (default: the source placement's; not the component or one inside it); in_place?, parent_path?: as occurrence.copy; translate?: [x,y,z]. Reassigned external bodies become base geometry; retained external links and omitted boundary joints are reported

label: Move Occurrence
params: occurrence; path?: exact placement; space?: local|world (default local); translate?: [x,y,z]; axis?: [x,y,z], angle?: radians or "30 deg", origin?: [x,y,z]; matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (instead of translate/axis/angle/origin: a rigid move as a row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows; one that is a rotation only up to rounding is orthonormalised, a scale, shear or mirror is refused); tolerance?: largest accepted |RᵀR − I| (default 1e-9, at most 1e-3); capture?: bool (default true; false keeps it pending until Capture Position); move_grounded?: bool (default false: a grounded occurrence refuses; true moves it and it stays grounded). Nested occurrence definitions remain shared

label: Drag Occurrence
params: occurrence or path: exact placement; at: [x,y,z] world point on it; point: [x,y,z] where it goes. Moves the placement by point - at (with any chain of joints it is in that is joined to nothing grounded) and captures its position; other pending moves stay pending. Shared definitions move in all placements. Grounded parts and parts joints hold to something fixed are refused (joint.reach moves those)

label: Align Occurrence
params: occurrence?, occurrences?, path?, paths?: placements to move together; from | from_face | from_plane; to | to_face | to_plane; flip?: bool; capture?: bool (default true); move_grounded?: bool (default false). Moves only the chosen occurrence placements in world coordinates without changing shared component geometry; a placement inside a component placed more than once moves in every placement of it, and the reply's `shared` lists those paths

label: Ground
params: occurrence; grounded?: bool (default toggles)

label: Move to Component
params: occurrence; path?: exact placement; parent: component id or name (0 or "root" for the design); parent_path?: the parent's placement to place it by (default: its only one, else the active one; every instance of the parent gets it). The placement keeps its world position; a move that would break a feature is refused

label: Capture Position
params: keeps pending occurrence moves

label: Revert Position
params: occurrences?: [ids] (default all); drops selected pending occurrence moves

label: Insert Design
params: path: a .sc design → a new component linked to it, holding its solid bodies as placed in that design and a copy of its design properties; name? (default: the design's name); parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); translate?: [x,y,z] in mm from the destination parent's origin (default [0,0,0], also with reuse); reuse?: bool (default false): insert a free occurrence, reusing an existing link to the same file when available

label: Update Links
params: component?: id or name (default: every linked component); components?: a list of ids or names, which goes on past a design it cannot read (that one keeps its bodies, is named in failed and gets a warning) — reads the linked designs again and replaces their bodies where they changed, as one undo step; → updated, unchanged, failed ([{component, name, error}]), warnings (also joints whose faces are gone or that no longer solve)

label: Relink Source
params: component: id or name of a linked component; path: a saved design (.sc or .json) — replaces the source and linked bodies for all its occurrences, preserving identities and placements; returns path, previous_path, warnings, joint_errors and joint_conflicts

label: Break Link
params: component: id or name of a linked component — keeps its bodies as they are and forgets the design file

label: Extract to File
params: component: id or name of a component that is not linked; path: the .sc design to write → its history, subcomponents and their joints move to that design, and the component becomes linked to it (as component.insert_design makes it); returns path, file, feature, bodies, notices (what stays behind), warnings and copies (components that build the same bodies: see component.replace_with_link)

label: Find Identical Copies
params: component: id or name of a linked component → copies: [{component, name}], the components not linked whose own history builds the same bodies

label: Replace with Link
params: component or components: [ids or names] of components that are not linked; with: a linked component, or path: a .sc design (its link here, else a new linked component) → each component's history goes and its placements become placements of the linked component; refused when its bodies are not the same as the link's; returns component, name, replaced and warnings

label: List Links
params: → linked components: component, name, path, file (resolved), found (null when the file is on a network location not allowed, or names a device: it is not looked for), changed (whether the file is no longer what this design last read: Update Links reads it again; null when not found or the link is older than this record), and then host (the network location) and reason

label: Joint Origin
params: name?, occurrence?: id|name (default: from the pick, or the named face's component), face: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a planar face) | circle: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a round end: a point on its wall or rim, the end's centre, or the round face's name as model.faces lists it) | edge: [x,y,z] (a point on an edge of a planar face: the edge's middle, z out of the face, y into it; on?: [x,y,z] a point on the face (default: the larger planar face beside the edge); corner?: [x,y,z] near one end: the corner there, x and y along its two edges into the face; found again by name, so it follows the face as it changes size; z?: [x,y,z] the frame's z instead of the face's normal, along the edge when it runs that way, x chosen from z: an edge or corner picked as it is, kept as a point where it can't be found by name) | point: [x,y,z], z?: [x,y,z]; a circle's z?: [x,y,z] (a round edge's centre with the way out of it: its end by name when that is the frame it shows, else a point there); body?: the named face's body; end?: "<name>" (a circle's end: the face across its rim there; default the end nearer the pick); x?: [x,y,z] (a direction, world) | "<face name>" | {face: [x,y,z]} (the frame's x: a direction, a plane's normal, or the way to another hole's axis; keeps a round origin's turn; a point's x is a direction, laid square to its z, default: chosen from z alone). Faces are kept by name: the origin follows its face, and a circle its end, when the design changes

label: Joint
params: type: rigid|revolute|slider|cylindrical|pin_slot|planar|ball, or a relation: parallel|perpendicular|angle|point_on_plane|point_on_line|line_on_plane (ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are; several between two parts add up); a, b: joint origins ({occurrence, face|circle|edge|point: [x,y,z] in world, or face|circle: "<face name>"; z? for a point, end?, x? as joint.origin} | origin name); values?: [angles in deg or expressions, distances]; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; flip?: bool (default false: the origins are mated, b's z against a's as two faces meet; true: b's z along a's, so two origins given at one point with the same z and x stay as they are; a point origin without x takes its x from z, so give x on both, or use joint.as_built, to keep a turned part where it is); offset?: mm or an expression; angle?: deg or an expression (an angle relation's tilt from mated; for other joints the default is none, or a half turn where that turns b less, so faces that already meet stay as they are); name?; quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed). An expression (text) is kept with the joint and worked out again whenever the design changes, so the joint follows the parameters it names; a joint whose expression no longer works out (a parameter deleted) is left out of the solve with the reason in its errors

label: As-Built Joint
params: type, a: occurrence, b: occurrence (stay where they are); at?: joint origin (default: b's origin) — the joint's frame; one on a or b is kept on its face or hole there, so the joint follows it as the design changes; name?; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; quiet?: bool

label: Rigid Group
params: occurrences: [ids or names] (move together, as they are)

label: Drive Joints

label: Interference
params: bodies?: [names] (default: all, in world placement; a name that is no body is refused); budget_s?: seconds (default 240, at most 86400: pairs not finished by then are listed in unchecked as "not checked: the time budget … ran out" and the call returns) → interferences: pairs that overlap with the overlap volume, area, bounding box and centre (a pin a hair off the axis of a hole of its size also has near_coaxial: {offset_mm, length_mm}, its volume the crescent the walls share); unchecked: [{a, b, reason}], the pairs that could not be checked, with the reason, and each mesh body (STL, 3MF or OBJ import: not intersected) as {a: name, b: null, reason: "mesh body: not checked"}, so count: 0 is not read as no overlap (checked counts the solid bodies). Bodies are pruned by bounding box first, then by their display meshes (pairs whose meshes stay apart by more than their chord tolerances, neither inside the other, are clear without a boolean), so any number of bodies is fine; the pairs left are intersected exactly, in parallel on desktop, the slowest first; at most 20000 pairs whose boxes overlap are intersected per call (truncated: true and skipped_pairs: n say when more were left out). Also: pairs_candidate (boxes overlap), pairs_cleared (by the meshes), pairs_intersected, pairs_not_checked, budget_exceeded, threads (worker threads; 0: on the calling thread), boolean_ms and tessellate_ms (kernel time summed over the pairs), slowest: [{a, b, ms, boolean_ms, tessellate_ms}] and ms

params: position: number of features to keep active, or "end" (omit = end) | feature: id|name (the marker goes right after it)

label: Reorder Feature
params: feature: id|name, position: its new index, active?: bool (true = it ends up before the history marker, false = behind it; other features keep their state); refused when a feature that worked would fail, unless allow_errors?: bool (default false): then made, and broken: [{feature, error}] lists the features it broke

label: Reorder Features
params: features: [id|name], position: insertion slot in the current history; selected features keep their relative order; active?: bool (as timeline.reorder's); refused when a feature that worked would fail, unless allow_errors?: bool (default false): then made, and broken: [{feature, error}] lists the features it broke

label: Edit Feature
params: feature: id|name, command: the feature's command id, params: its parameters (the feature is rebuilt in place) → feature, recomputed, restored, rolled_back: bool (the feature is after the history marker, so the edit is not built yet; `note` then says so), warning?

label: Feature Dependents
params: feature: id|name → features deleted with it, and features that would fail without it

label: Suppress Feature
params: feature: id|name | features: [id|name] | groups: [timeline folder ids] (every feature and joint in those folders and their nested folders; one undo step), suppressed?: bool (default toggles: features and joints are all suppressed unless all of them already are, then all are unsuppressed) → feature: id (or features: [ids]; groups: [ids] and joints: [ids] when groups are given), suppressed

label: Edit Feature
params: feature: id|name, set: {fields to change, merged into the feature's definition as timeline.inspect returns it, e.g. {"extent": {"distance": "30"}} (extrude), {"angle": "90 deg"} (revolve); a dotted key names a nested field ({"plane.distance": "8 mm"} = {"plane": {"distance": "8 mm"}}); expressions are text, or a number in mm or degrees} → recomputed: features rebuilt, restored: features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused

label: Inspect Feature
params: group: folder id → group, name, parent, features, joints; or feature: id|name → type, definition (the fields timeline.edit's set changes, with their current values), inputs: [{label, param, expression, unit}] (named inputs parameters.change can also set), error, warning

label: Select
params: items: [{type: body|edge|face|feature|sketch_curve|sketch_point|profile, …}], add?: bool; face/edge: body plus point [x,y,z] in world mm or index (both also accepted); a point uses Measure's pick tolerance, an index supplies a point on the item; invalid partial picks leave the selection unchanged

label: Selection filter
params: mode: body|face|component → validated UI pick granularity; headless echo only, no document edits or undo

label: Select Same Look
params: body?: world body name, face?: face index; defaults to the current body/face selection → selects objects using the resolved appearance

label: Copy Features
params: features: [ids or names] (in timeline order on paste)

label: Paste Features
params: translate?: [x,y,z] (moves the copies' geometry); component?: where the copies go (default: the active one), component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one); the copies go at the marker, each where its original is in the world (copies into their own component keep its coordinates); body transfers are left out; from_design?: true to paste sketch features from the host's cross-design clipboard snapshot

label: Copy Sketch Entities
params: entities?: [curve or point ids] (default: the selected sketch geometry); the constraints and dimensions among them come along

label: Cut Sketch Entities
params: entities?: [curve or point ids] (default: the selected sketch geometry): copies them as sketch.copy does, then deletes them (one undo step)

label: Paste Sketch Entities
params: at?: [x, y] (sketch point the copy's centre goes to) | translate?: [x, y]; without either, offset from the original in its own sketch and at the same coordinates in another; sketch?: target (default: the active sketch)

label: Add Recorded Feature
params: feature: a feature as the design file and timeline.inspect hold it ({type, name?, id?, …}; the name is kept even when another feature has it, the id is kept and refused when another feature has it, so later steps can refer to them); params?: [{name, expression, unit?, comment?}] (the model parameters its sketch dimensions use); the feature goes at the marker → feature, name, error, warning

label: Export Command Script
params: path?: write the script to this file → script: {commands: [...]} that rebuilds the design (solidcraft-cli eval/run), steps, omitted: what the script leaves out (appearances, folders, views, configurations, print-face assignments); components and assemblies are not supported yet

label: Change Parameters
params: name, expression (number or text), unit?: mm|cm|m|in|ft|deg|rad|""|text (new parameters default to their value's unit, a length the design's units; a text parameter's expression is its text, quotes round it optional: sketch texts' words are built from it), comment?, favorite?: bool, new_name?: rename (references follow; an expression `new = value` renames to `new` and sets value, or sets `new` when the expression is just `new`); or delete: name; or changes: {name: expression, …} (existing parameters, checked together and rebuilt once, all or nothing) → changed?: {name: value} (with changes), recomputed: features rebuilt, restored: features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused (e.g. a value set back), switched?: [{feature, name, suppressed}] (the configuration rules that switch a feature's suppression and read a parameter whose value changed run in their order, as on activation; driven parameters and restrictions wait for a configuration edit or activation)

label: List Parameters
params: favorites?: bool (only favourites), filter?: all|user|sketch|feature|favorites → parameters (name, expression, unit, value (mm/deg in every reply), display_value (in its own unit), source, feature/input, comment, favorite, uses, used_by, error) and cycles

label: Add User Parameter
params: name, expression, unit?: as parameters.change (text: a text parameter, its expression the text), comment?, favorite?: bool

label: Rename Parameter
params: name, new_name (expressions, feature inputs and dimensions that use it follow)

label: Delete Parameter
params: name (refused while something uses it; the error lists the users)

label: Favorite Parameter
params: name, favorite?: bool (default true)

label: Move Parameter
params: name, before | after: another user parameter; the user parameter is listed just before or after it

label: Comment Parameter
params: name, comment

label: Parameter Users
params: name → users (parameters, feature inputs, dimensions) and the features it drives

label: Parameter Graph
params: → nodes, edges [user, used] (users include Feature:<name>), cycles, errors

label: Export Parameters
params: format?: csv|json (default csv, or from the path), path?: write to a file → text

label: Import Parameters
params: text: CSV (header with name, expression, unit?, comment?) or JSON [{name, expression, unit?, comment?}] | path; all or nothing

label: Evaluate Expression
params: expression, kind?: length|angle|unitless (or unit?: mm|in|deg…; text: the text a text parameter would hold, as `text`) → ok, value (mm/rad), display_value, references, error

label: Complete Expression
params: prefix?: the text before the cursor → word, suggestions [{text, kind: parameter|function|unit|constant, detail}]

label: Parameter Sweep
params: parameter: name; values: [number | expression] (at most 200) | from, to: numbers, steps? (default 10, at most 199: steps + 1 values) → for each value, in a copy of the design (the design itself is not changed): {value, ms (the rebuild), ok, failed: [{feature, name, error}], warned: [{feature, name, warning}] (features that build at the current value and fail or warn at this one), joints_lost: [{joint, name, origin?: a|b, why}], joints_flipped: [{joint, name, origin: a|b, degrees}] (an origin's z turned more than 90° on its own part from where it is now), sketches_flipped: [{sketch, name, degrees}] (the sketch plane's normal turned more than 90°), sketches_failed: [{sketch, name, failing, folded}] (a solve that fails, or keeps a triangle's turn or an offset's side only by flipping it)} (or {value, ms, ok: false, error} where the parameter takes no such value); summary: {values, ok, slowest_ms, failed, joints_lost, joints_flipped, sketches_flipped, sketches_failed} (how many values show each)

label: New Design
params: name?

label: Open
params: path: .sc design (or a .solidcraft design from an earlier release), .dxf/.svg drawing (opens as a new, unsaved design with an XY sketch, using sketch.insert_dxf/sketch.insert_svg units and defaults), or a .step/.stp/.igs/.fcstd/.3dm/.3mf/.stl/.obj/.glb/.gltf file (STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino, 3MF, STL, OBJ or glTF; opens as a new design holding the file as a component named after it, as file.insert_step and file.insert_mesh make), or a .ply/.xyz/.pts point cloud (opens as a new design holding it, as pointcloud.insert makes; its `units` and `max_points` as there); up?: z|y for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino or glTF file (see file.insert_step and file.insert_mesh); names?: auto|solid|product|instance for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file (see file.insert_step); read_only?: bool (a design: saving to its own file is refused, file.save_as keeps the changes elsewhere) → open_elsewhere: {host, user, app, opened} when another SolidCraft has the design open (its lock file is fresh)

label: Insert STEP
params: path: STEP, IGES, FreeCAD .FCStd or Rhino .3dm file (its bodies join the design as an Import base feature in a new component named after the file, placed in the active component; an assembly's products become nested components, a repeated part one component with an occurrence per placement, all held as one rigid group until component.unlock → component, component_name, occurrence, subcomponents?, rigid_joints?); name? (the feature's and the component's); up?: z|y (default z: the file's axes are kept; y: the file has Y up, so the import's component is turned a quarter turn about X, Y becoming Z → stand_up: its occurrence); names?: auto|solid|product|instance (default auto: keep meaningful solid names, replace placeholders with the nearest named product, else instance; solid: the solid's own name; product: the part's name; instance: the occurrence's name, else the product's); matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (where the new component's occurrence sits in the active component, after `up`: a rigid row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows, as occurrence.move takes it; a scale, shear or mirror is refused before the file is read); tolerance? (see occurrence.move)

label: Insert Mesh
params: path: .3mf, .stl, .obj, .ply (with faces), .glb or .gltf file (its meshes join the design as mesh bodies in a new component named after the file → component, component_name, occurrence; a glTF file's node tree becomes nested components held as one rigid group until component.unlock, a mesh placed again another occurrence, its materials the bodies' appearances, and its metres millimetres); name?; up?: z|y for a glTF file (default y: glTF has Y up, so the import's component is turned a quarter turn about X, Y becoming Z → stand_up: its occurrence; z: the file's axes are kept)

label: Save
params: path? (default: current file; a name that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (replace the design's file even though another program or computer changed it since it was opened or saved; without it that save is refused)

label: Save As
params: path (a design file name, .sc as a rule; one that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (as file.save, when `path` is the design's own file)

label: Recoverable Designs
params: dir? (default: the recovery folder) → designs autosaved by apps that crashed or closed with unsaved changes

label: Recover Design
params: id (from doc.recovery_list); dir?; discard?: bool (delete the entry once open) — opens it with its file path, unsaved

label: Discard Recovered Design
params: id, or all: true; dir?

label: Export
params: path; format?: stl|stla|obj|step|3mf|3mf-tagged|urdf|json (default from extension; 3mf-tagged: 3MF whose triangles carry their B-rep face, at full precision, for meshing and analysis tools; docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md; obj: the colours of the bodies go in a material library (`.mtl`) written next to the mesh file; urdf: the whole assembly as a robot, with STL meshes written next to it; docs/urdf.md); bodies?: [names] (JSON and URDF export the complete design); urdf only: mesh_prefix? (before each mesh file name, e.g. package://robot/meshes/), effort? (default 1000), velocity? (default 10); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ and 3MF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts)

label: Export STEP
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body; a design with components then exports as a STEP assembly) → {path, bytes, format}: STEP, whatever the path's extension

label: Export STL
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body); quality?: standard|fine|finest (default standard) → {path, bytes, format}: binary STL, whatever the path's extension

label: Export 3MF
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body); quality?: standard|fine|finest (default standard); objects?: body|component (as file.export) → {path, bytes, format}: 3MF, whatever the path's extension

label: Export OBJ
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body); quality?: standard|fine|finest (default standard) → {path, bytes, format, files}: OBJ, with the colours of the bodies in a material library (`.mtl`) next to it

label: Export URDF
params: path; mesh_prefix?; effort? (default 1000); velocity? (default 10) → {path, format, files, links, joints, warnings}: the whole assembly as a robot, with STL meshes written next to it; docs/urdf.md

label: Save As Mesh
params: path; format?: stl|3mf|3mf-tagged (default from the extension, else stl; 3mf-tagged: docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md); bodies?: [names] (default: all); ascii?: bool (STL); slicer?: id or name from file.slicers, the program path it lists, or a program the user added under Custom… (send the saved file there, through the same steps as file.send_to_slicer: a slicer that has to be started first is waited for; may be deprecated later in favour of file.send_to_slicer or a Send to App workflow, kept for scripts); single_instance?: bool (default true; see file.send_to_slicer); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ and 3MF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts)

label: Send to Slicer
params: slicer: id or name from file.slicers, or a program the user added under Custom…; bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); wait?: block|return|no (default block: a slicer that drops a file at a cold start is started alone and the call waits up to 10 s for it to be ready, then sends; return: start it and answer {starting}; no: send now); single_instance?: bool (default true: PrusaSlicer, SuperSlicer and Cura load the file in the window that is open); format?: 3mf|stl|3mf-tagged (default 3mf, in millimetres; STL if that can't be written) → saves the bodies in this user's slicer folder and opens the file in the slicer. The file name stays the same for the same design and bodies, so sending again replaces it (use the slicer's Reload from disk)

label: Open with EasyPrint
params: consent: bool (required: true only once the user has agreed to upload the model to Printables' servers; it stays there for 30 minutes and opening it needs a Printables sign-in); bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); format?: 3mf|stl (default 3mf, in millimetres) → uploads the bodies to EasyPrint, Printables' slicer in the browser, and opens it in the browser. 100 MB at most. Works in the desktop app and the browser build; the CLI has no way to upload yet

label: Installed Slicers
params: → the slicers found on this machine: [{id, name, program, icon?}]; pass an id, a name or the program path as file.send_to_slicer's or file.save_mesh's `slicer`

label: Print Face
params: body: its name; point?: [x, y, z] on a flat face of it, in mm (omit to clear) → {body, face?}: marks the face a slicer export (file.send_to_slicer, file.save_mesh with slicer, file.open_in_easyprint) lays the body on: turned so the face points down at Z = 0, the centre of mass over the origin. One per body, replacing the last; flat faces of solid bodies only. A print face that is gone or no longer flat is reported in the export's warnings, and the body exported as it lies

label: Design Properties
params: → metadata: the design's metadata object as saved (other tools' keys too); properties: each of SolidCraft's design properties (project, part number, revision…), its text or null (absent, or not text)

label: Change Design Properties
params: key and value, or values: {key: value, …} (all or nothing, one undo step). SolidCraft's keys, the ones document.metadata's properties lists, take text ("" or null removes); another tool's data goes under its reverse-DNS key such as com.example.tool (an object; null removes) → metadata, changed: [keys]

label: Remove Design Property
params: key, or keys: [keys] (any key, also one another tool wrote) → metadata, removed: [keys that were there]

label: Enable Component Colors
params: enabled?: bool (omitted: toggle); temporary component colours, without changing appearances

label: Measure
params: bodies?: [names] (default all); names_only?: bool (each world body's name and its definition's, nothing measured) → closed per body; volume_mm3, center_of_mass, density_g_cm3 and mass_g only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; area, bbox and counts for all; total.open_bodies_skipped counts bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; or items: [1-2 selections] (face/edge: type, body, point; index optional) → length/area/volume; diameter, radius, circumference or arc_length/angle_deg of circles, arcs and cylinders; slot sizes; min (distance_mm, from, to), max, center_distance (centre to centre, or from an axis) and angle

label: Inspect Design
params: measure?: bool (include body measurements)

label: Design Revision
params: → document_id (this open design's id: kept while it stays open, another for each design started or opened), revision (moves whenever the design, what is hidden or a component's uncaptured position changes, never on a selection or a view; from one counter for the whole run, so it never repeats). Read-only

label: Inspect Sketch
params: sketch?: id|name (default active)

label: List Edges
params: body: name

label: List Faces
params: body: name → per face: index, name (what face.delete, sheet.convert `face`, solid.shell … take in place of a point), exact, area, centroid (not always on the face), plane_normal, point (a point on the face that picks it), cylinder? ({origin, axis, radius} of a cylindrical face), sheet_face? (a folded sheet's face: `sheet:<body>:<panel>:<side>`, panel base or a flange's tag F<feature>.<k>, side top | bottom | rim.<edge> | bend.inner | bend.outer; taken wherever a face name is, and it holds while sizes change and flanges come and go)

label: Physical Material
params: bodies: [names]; material: name (Steel, Aluminum, ABS Plastic, …, or one made with material.create; `material.list`)

label: Appearance
params: bodies?: [names]; faces?: [[x,y,z] on faces] (body?: which body, default the nearest); components?: [names or ids, or occurrence names]; appearance?: library name or stable starter.* ID (appearance.library) | color: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1, default 1); name?: inert copied look label (requires color, mutually exclusive with appearance); pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (requires color/appearance and opacity 1); a starter ID or registered starter name resolves its recipe before color overrides; omitted pbr retains that response and pbr: null explicitly clears it. Unavailable glass recipes refuse through either selector. Other custom labels with an explicit color retain legacy scalar behavior. Neither appearance nor color (or color: null): clear, so the face follows its body, the body its component, the component its material

label: Copy Look
params: target: appearance.chain target. Copies its resolved look to a transient session clipboard. No document change or dialogs.

label: Paste Look
params: bodies/faces/components: appearance.assign targets. Applies the copied look atomically in one undo step; no dialogs.

label: Favorite Look
params: look: appearance.assign look; favorite: bool → validated look and preference request; UI library preference only, no document change or dialogs.

label: Appearance Chain
params: target: {body: name} | {body: name, face: zero-based model.faces index} | {component: name or id}; a placed copy's name (`KB (K:2)`, `K:2`) means the body or component it shows. Returns steps [{step: face|body|component|material, look: {name,color,opacity,pbr?} or null}] in precedence order and active (step or null). Component material is the common default look of its directly owned bodies, null if mixed/empty. Imported paint is a display fallback outside the four steps. Read-only; no dialogs

label: Replace Appearance
params: from: library name | saved look {name,color,opacity,pbr?} (copy appearance.list in_design); to: library name | assignment look {appearance? | color, name?, opacity?, pbr?} (appearance.assign rules; no clear). Matches the full look including name and PBR. scope?: {bodies?: [names], components?: [names or ids]} (a placed copy's name means the body or component it shows), at most 10000 targets; body scope includes face overrides, component scope selects only the component override. Omitted scope means all overrides, including hidden/suppressed ones; physical defaults are unchanged. Duplicate targets count once. Returns count of rewritten overrides; zero adds no history. One undo step, atomic; no dialogs. Designs above 100000 overrides refuse

label: Appearance Library
params: → 20 legacy scalar appearances, six opaque PBR finishes and 40 starter recipes with IDs, categories, provenance, requirements and availability; six starter glass recipes are unavailable

label: List Appearances
params: body?: name (or a placed copy's, `KB (K:2)`: the body it shows) → assigned appearances; with body, its resolved look and its faces' (face index, look)

label: List Materials
params: → built-in and design-owned materials (user: true, look, optional physical_card/physical_validation/density_comparison). Read-only; candidate engineering records do not certify sources or supply a solver

label: Describe Command
params: command: a command id. Returns {id, label, params, input, output} (and param_warnings in the warn parameter-check mode): the command's parameter documentation and, once the command has a typed contract, the JSON Schemas (2020-12) of its parameters and of a successful result (null otherwise). Read-only.

label: Compare Bodies
params: a, b: body names (default: the two selected bodies, or the design's only two), in world placement; tolerance?: mm (0.001 to 10, default 0.01): surfaces closer than this agree; spacing?: mm (default 0.5): the largest piece of a face sampled as one point, coarser for a body that would need more than max_points? (default 8 million, up to 50 million) samples; max_regions? (default 50); color?: true | {only_in_a?, only_in_b?: "#rrggbb"} (colours the faces that hold a region, red where only a has material and green where only b has: the faces mostly beyond the tolerance, else the one with the largest share; an undo step) → a, b: volume_mm3, area_mm2, center_of_mass, bbox; difference: b − a; deviation: a_to_b, b_to_a (max_mm, mean_mm, at, area_beyond_mm2); regions, largest first: side (only_in_a | only_in_b), volume_mm3 (integrated along lines through the region: resolution), area_mm2, max_deviation_mm, at, center, bbox, faces_a, faces_b (face indices, as model.faces lists them); identical; verdict; warnings (a body whose surface does not enclose what it measures, lines left out). Works from the two surfaces, without a boolean of the bodies, so near-identical bodies compare too

label: Compare Picture
params: reference: path to a PNG or JPEG the model should match; view?/camera?/bodies?/rows? as inspect.silhouette; crop_px?: [x, y, w, h] in pixels, or crop_fraction?: [x, y, w, h] as fractions 0..1 of the picture (to take one view off a board); part_fills_crop?: false — with true the crop box is the part itself and no background search runs, for a crop that tightly frames the part; fit?: "width" | "height" | "both" (default "width"): one uniform scale, taken from the named dimension ("both" claims both and scales by width, reporting aspect_mismatch when the shapes differ); overlay?: false leaves the overlay PNG out → overlap (0..1), edges: top|bottom|left|right in mm at nine stations (positive where the model reaches past the picture, null where a station misses one of the two), the grid and its mm_per_px, and overlay_png (red model, blue picture) as base64 PNG. The compare is outline only: holes are not compared — both the picture's and the model's holes are filled

label: Silhouette
params: view?: front|back|left|right|top|bottom|iso (default front); or camera?: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?} (mm, radians; fov 0 means parallel); bodies?: [world body names] (default visible bodies, named hidden bodies included); rows?: mask height in pixels (default 240, clamped to 16..1024) → tightly framed run-length mask, box_mm, mm_per_px, right/up, projection, body and triangle counts

label: New Physical Material
params: name (not a built-in material's); density_g_cm3: (0, 1000]; appearance?: library name (appearance.library) | color?: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1), pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (opaque only, needs color/appearance): the default look. A named appearance keeps its preset response when pbr is omitted; pbr: null selects scalar shading. Optical edits do not change density. physical_card?: validated SI candidate record (null/omitted means unknown); card density never changes assigned density. Assign it with material.assign

label: Edit Physical Material
params: material: a material defined in this design; name? (bodies and configuration cells follow); density_g_cm3?; appearance? | color?, opacity?, pbr? (as material.create; color: null clears the look). physical_card?: validated SI candidate record (omitted retains, null clears). Omitted appearance/color retains the entire current look

label: Inspect Physical Material
params: material: built-in or design-owned name. Returns assigned density, default appearance, optional physical_card, validation and density comparison. Read-only; missing engineering data remains unknown and card density does not change mass

label: Delete Physical Material
params: material: a material defined in this design; replace?: material for the bodies and configuration cells that use it (without it, a material in use is refused)

label: Validate Physical Material Data
params: card: schema_version 1 engineering material card in SI units. Returns numerical consistency, derived isotropic moduli, missing conditions and sources needing review. Read-only; does not assign/save properties or provide an analysis solver. See docs/physical-material-cards.md

label: Directional Elastic Modulus
params: card: schema_version 1 engineering material card; direction: three finite nonzero-vector components in the card's material-local axes. Returns normalized direction, Young modulus in Pa and source/condition review. Read-only constitutive query; no structural solver, persistence or body-axis assignment. See docs/physical-material-cards.md

label: Inspect Local Library
params: path: v1/v2 library JSON; returns validated catalog and exact entry revisions, without changing the design

label: Export Design Library
params: path: .json; id? (default user.local), name?, provenance?, overwrite? false, format? solidcraft-library/2 (default) | solidcraft-library/1 (refuses PBR/cards). Copies assigned looks and design-local physical definitions; never changes the design

label: Apply Local Library Entry
params: path, entry: qualified ID, revision: exact content SHA-256; targets?: {bodies?, faces?: [{body,point}], components?}; name?: physical material name on import. Copies values in one undo step; material conflicts are explicit

label: Section Analysis
params: plane: XY|XZ|YZ | construction plane name or id | {origin, normal}; offset?: expr along the plane's normal (XY: +Z, XZ: +Y, YZ: +X); at?: expr, the cut's world coordinate on the named plane's axis (XY: Z, XZ: Y, YZ: X), instead of offset; flip?: bool; hatch?: bool (hatch the cut faces, in each body's colour; default true); or clear: true. Returns the cut's origin and normal, and for a named plane its axis and at

label: Viewport Status Details
params: no parameters → current effect settings/detail capabilities and retained per-seam Continuity diagnostics, with current geometry validity; read-only, no evaluation
